subject: Whistic short-form: remediation playbook + targeted evidence backfill
body:
From: Evan Rogers <evan.rogers@cedarhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Whistic profile — expedited ask for procurement window

Hi Kimberly,

We’re in the final stages of Cedar Health’s procurement review and the security team requested a completed Whistic profile and a short SIG/CAIQ extract by 3/20. They specifically called out: SOC 2 status, encryption-at-rest details, IAM control owner, and evidence for logging/retention (S3 + CloudTrail snapshots).

Is there a lean approach you can run with us that doesn’t require a full SIG import? Our buyer (security) is comfortable with a focused evidence backfill for the controls that matter for patient-data adjacency.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Rogers
Director, Procurement
Cedar Health

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Evan Rogers <evan.rogers@cedarhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Whistic profile — expedited ask for procurement window

Hi Evan —

We can do a short-form remediation + evidence backfill that targets the controls your security team flagged. Plan in brief: 

1) Rapid control triage (today — 24 hrs): confirm which controls Cedar’s reviewer needs as "must have" vs "nice to have."
2) Evidence harvest (2 business days): pull SOC2 attestation, KMS key metadata, S3 retention policy, CloudTrail snapshots, IAM role inventory exports.
3) Whistic update (1 business day): upload evidence stubs and short-answer text to the profile; mark remaining answers as "remediation in progress" with ETA.
4) Executive summary for procurement (same day): one-page control matrix + links to evidence.

I’ve looped Marcus and Mina — Marcus can advise on the logs/exports, Mina will owner SOC2/SIG mapping, and Priyom will coordinate uploads to Whistic.

We’ll attach a playbook and example evidence naming convention. Evan — can you confirm the exact controls (or share the security reviewer’s checklist) so we don’t duplicate effort?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Vendor Security Lead | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Evan Rogers <evan.rogers@cedarhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Whistic profile — expedited ask for procurement window

Quick technical notes:

- SOC2: attestation PDF is current (2026-09) and lives in secure drive; I’ll pull the specific page references.
- Encryption at rest: We use AES-256 (AWS KMS). I’ll provide the key policy excerpt and KMS alias.
- Logging: CloudTrail is multi-region and immutable; S3 lifecycle + versioning enabled on prod buckets. I can export a 90-day activity snapshot (CSV) and a signed S3 manifest for proof.
- IAM: I’ll export role inventories and a list of service principals with last-used timestamps.

Attachments I’ll drop: whistic-screenshot-20270310.png (how we’ll label evidence), SIG_Mapping_CedarHealth.xlsx (starter control mapping).

Marcus
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Evan Rogers <evan.rogers@cedarhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Whistic profile — expedited ask for procurement window

Evan —

I started a control-to-evidence mapping in the attached SIG_Mapping_CedarHealth.xlsx. For the short-form push I recommend we focus on the following control families:

- Encryption (CC6.1, CC6.2) — KMS key policy + storage config screenshots
- Access Management (AC1.1, AC1.4) — IAM inventory + last-used export
- Logging & Monitoring (DM1.2) — CloudTrail snapshot + Splunk alert example
- Incident Response (IR) — IR runbook excerpt + contact list

If Cedar needs CAIQ snippets instead of SIG fields I can translate the key answers (3–4 fields) for the Whistic Q&A. Priyom — can you confirm you have API access to Cedar’s Whistic team or should we request an upload link?

-Mina
Security Programs Manager

---
From: Whistic Support <support@whistic.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API access and bulk evidence upload

Hi Priyom / Kim,

We confirm Cedar Health’s buyer account (cedarhealth-12345) has delegated upload access. For bulk uploads you can use the profile import endpoint: POST https://api.whistic.com/v1/profiles/{profile_id}/artifacts. We accept PDF, PNG, CSV.

We created a temporary API token that will expire in 48 hours. Use the token for the bulk import and then rotate after completion.

Support
Whistic.com

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Evan Rogers <evan.rogers@cedarhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Whistic Support <support@whistic.com>, Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@sec-consult.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Whistic short-form: remediation playbook + targeted evidence backfill

Summary and next steps (action owners):

1) Evan / Cedar security: confirm must-have control list by COB Mon 3/14.
2) Marcus: produce exports — CloudTrail 90-day snapshot, S3 manifest, IAM last-used — due 3/15 EOD.
3) Mina: finalize SIG-to-Whistic Q&A extract and mark CAIQ snippets — due 3/15 noon.
4) Priyom: perform bulk upload to Cedar profile using Whistic token, attach evidence with naming convention; rotate token immediately after — target 3/16 morning.
5) Kim: draft one-page control matrix and procurement summary (remediation-playbook-v1.pdf attached) — will send to Cedar when uploads complete.

Attachments included: remediation-playbook-v1.pdf, SIG_Mapping_CedarHealth.xlsx, whistic-screenshot-20270310.png

Evan — if that timeline works I’ll park a short Zoom on Mon 3/15 so we can run through any redlines before upload.

Thanks everyone —

Kim
Kimberly Park
Vendor Security Lead | Redwood Inference
